source_text: Ζητήσας δὲ μεμελημένος, καὶ σοφῶς κατανοήσας τὴν περὶ γῆν φύσιν ἅπασαν, ποικιλωτάτην ἔγνων, ὡς ἀνθρώπῳ δέδοται πονεῖν ἐπὶ γῆς, ἄλλοτε ἀλλοίᾳ καμάτου προφάσει ἐγκαλινδουμένῳ εἰς τὸ μηδέν. Πνεύματος δὲ ἀλλοκότου καὶ μυσαροῦ τὰ κάτω ἅπαντα πλήθει, ὥστε μὴ εἶναι αὐτὰ ἀνακτήσασθαι, ἀλλὰ μηδὲ ἀναθυμηθῆναι τὸ παράπαν ὅση τὰ κατὰ ἀνθρώπους πράγματα κατείληφεν ἀτοπία. Λογισάμενος γάρ ποτε ἐγὼ κατ᾽ ἐμαυτόν, καὶ οἰηθεὶς ὡς ἁπάντων εἴην τότε τῶν πρὸ ἐμαυτοῦ γεγονότων ἐνταυθοῖ σοφώτερος· ἔγνων παραβολάς τε συνεῖναι καὶ πραγμάτων φύσεις. ᾨήθην δὲ τηνάλλως ἐπὶ τούτῳ φέρεσθαι, καὶ σοφίᾳ μὲν γνῶσιν ἕπεσθαι, γνώσει δὲ πόνους ἐπακολουθεῖν.
thought_title: Solomon recounts his exhaustive inquiry into earthly life and its futility
orientation: Solomon describes his personal investigation of all activity under the sun, finding it wearisome, irrecoverable, and marked by a perverse spirit, concluding that wisdom brings knowledge but knowledge brings pain.
pass_a_gloss: Having sought while taking care, and having understood wisely the whole nature concerning the earth, I knew it to be most varied, as it is given to a human being to toil upon the earth, rolling about from time to time with a different pretext of toil into nothing. And a strange and filthy spirit fills all the things below, so that they are not able to be recovered, but not even to be recalled at all, so much strangeness has seized the things according to humans. For having reasoned once within myself, and having supposed that I was then wiser than all those who had come to be before me here; I knew comparisons to hold together and the natures of things. I thought to be carried differently upon this, and that wisdom is followed by knowledge, but by knowledge pains are followed.

lemmas.gloss: to recall / call back to mind

choices.why: Perfect middle participle of μελέτω, 'to care for, attend to'; reflects Solomon's deliberate, careful search, not casual curiosity.
Present middle participle; depicts a person repeatedly turning over in toil with shifting pretexts, emphasizing restless futility.
ἀλλόκοτος = 'out of place, perverse'; μυσαροῦ = 'causing disgust, abominable'; together they personify a corrupting spirit over sub‑heavenly things.
Not mere 'absurdity' but a quality of being 'out of place' (ἄτοπος); the created order has become alien to its purpose.
In wisdom context, παραβολαί are analogies that make nature intelligible; 'parables' narrows the sense too far.

choices.term: σοφίᾳ μὲν γνῶσιν ἕπεσθαι, γνώσει δὲ πόνους ἐπακολουθεῖν
choices.english: wisdom is followed by knowledge, but by knowledge pains are followed
choices.why: Preserves the chiasmus and the grim sequence: wisdom → knowledge → pain; ἕπεσθαι and ἐπακολουθεῖν both mean 'follow' but the latter stresses attendant consequences.
rejected: wisdom brings knowledge, knowledge brings sorrow
knowledge follows wisdom, pain follows knowledge

bible_refs.note: ζητήσας … καὶ σοφῶς κατανοήσας parallels 'ἐζήτησα καὶ ἐξήτασα τῇ σοφίᾳ'
πᾶν τὸ γινόμενον ὑπὸ τὸν ἥλιον … πάντα μάταιον καὶ ποίμνην πνεύματος; here rendered as ἀλλοκότου καὶ μυσαροῦ πνεύματος
ἐγὼ ἐμεγάλυνσα τὴν σοφίαν … ἔγνων παραβολάς … καὶ ἐπιγνῶσιν
ὅτι ἐν πολῇ σοφίᾳ πολὺ γνῶσις, καὶ ὁ προσθέων γνῶσιν προσθήσει πόνον

pass_b_english: Solomon says: I searched carefully and understood wisely the whole nature of things on earth, and found it most varied. Human beings are given toil on earth, rolling about from one pretext of labor to another, ending in nothing. A strange and filthy spirit fills all things below, so that they cannot be recovered, nor even recalled to mind at all, such is the strangeness that has seized human affairs. For I once reasoned within myself, thinking I had become wiser than all who had come before me here; I came to know comparisons and the natures of things. I thought I was being carried along in vain on this course: knowledge follows wisdom, and toils follow knowledge.

problems.quote: I thought to make progress in this way
problems.source_quote: ᾨήθην δὲ τηνάλλως ἐπὶ τούτῳ φέρεσθαι
problems.why: τηνάλλως means 'in vain/idly'. The English turns a futile course into positive progress, reversing the sense.
problems.fix: I thought I was being carried along in vain on this course: knowledge follows wisdom, and toils follow knowledge.

problems.quote: but by knowledge pains are followed
problems.why: Toils follow knowledge. As written, knowledge seems to follow pains, and the clause is hard to parse.
problems.ruling: γνώσει δὲ πόνους ἐπακολουθεῖν means toils follow knowledge. 'By knowledge pains are followed' makes pains the thing followed, so it reverses the sequence.

edits.old: I thought to make progress in this way, that wisdom is followed by knowledge, but by knowledge pains are followed.
edits.new: I thought I was being carried along in vain on this course: knowledge follows wisdom, and toils follow knowledge.

fixed: Fixed 'I thought to make progress in this way' — source 'ᾠήθην δὲ τηνάλλως ἐπὶ τούτῳ φέρεσθαι' means 'I thought I was being carried along in vain on this course' (τηνάλλως = in vain/idly, not 'progress'). Also fixed 'but by knowledge pains are followed' — source 'γνώσει δὲ πόνους ἐπακολουθεῖν' means 'and toils follow knowledge' (active: toils follow knowledge, not passive 'pains are followed'). Combined into one natural sentence.

last_rejected.quote: I came to know comparisons and the natures of things.
last_rejected.source_quote: ἔγνων παραβολάς τε συνεῖναι καὶ πραγμάτων φύσεις.
last_rejected.why: ἔγνων with συνεῖναι means he knew how to understand them, not that he merely came to know them.
last_rejected.fix: I knew how to understand comparisons and the natures of things.
last_rejected.ruling: ἔγνων … συνεῖναι (know/understand) παραβολάς καὶ φύσεις: 'came to know comparisons and natures' keeps the sense; dropping the infinitive is a minor nuance, not a meaning change.
